Every claim its 171-line header makes that I could execute, I executed, and every one reproduced: exit 0 / FINDINGS: 0 on the live pinned bytes in 0.12s; all 14 shape-preserving meaning-inverting artifact mutations refused, including the ten escapes that rejected check-delivery-v4.py, reproduced byte-for-byte from that review's escape list; all 17 code mutations fail for their own named reason; the 277-position statement-seal domain derives from the artifact and equals STATEMENT_SEALS exactly both ways, with zero duplicate keys in the source dict and sample seal digests reproducing under my own independent NFC/sha256 pipeline; the append-a-false-sentence census reproduces its published figures exactly (989 distinct string leaves, 554 refused, 432 admitted, 3 unreachable) and 0 of the 432 admitted positions is sealed or inside a compiled block; my own falsity attacks outside the built-in suites (a published boolean flipped true, a published byte length moved by one, a committedBytesHex made odd-length) were each refused with a single finding naming the exact position in (recomputed, published) order, with no traceback. BOUNDARY: this verdict grants CHECKER STANDING ONLY. It does not apply delivery.v5.json, does not discharge the section 7.1 disqualifier on that candidate (which STANDS AT FULL STRENGTH per its own review, 1e5de421...), does not modify DELIVERY's freeze row, and does not close DR-011-R04 - it characterizes the fixture-skew half of R04 at fixtureSkewMeasured and leaves the successor-or-disposition decision, including OBS-1's retention, to the coordinator.

advisories.finding: A duplicate JSON key in the SUBJECT propagates as an uncaught DuplicateKey traceback at exit 1 rather than a formatted finding. The refusal is loud and NAMES the key (section 7.5 satisfied), but exit 1 is the same code the docstring assigns to 'findings', so a CI reader cannot distinguish 'subject has findings' from 'subject failed to parse' - the section 7.8.1 rule-3 shape one size smaller. The docstring states 'the count is printed on every run and --selftest requires it not to grow'. The second half is FALSE of the code: selftest() contains no assertion on danglingIntraDocumentPointers (measured: the identifier appears only at the bump site and in the docstring; no suite compares the count to its baseline of 3). Dangling pointers are notes, never findings, so growth would pass every suite silently. A one-line doc fix or a one-line selftest assertion closes it; recorded because a false sentence about what an instrument's own selftest enforces is the exact class this instrument exists to hunt.

The register names check-delivery-v5.py as DELIVERY's validator. Scope overstatement, measured: the register's nine DELIVERY invariants (DL-PROV, DL-ELIG, DL-SUPPLY, DL-PROF, DL-AIRGAP, DL-PLATFORM, DL-EXPL, DL-TM, DL-ASSURE) occur ZERO times in the instrument, and 'releaseFixtures' occurs ZERO times. reviewerStatement: I set out to make this instrument pass on wrong bytes, using the same posture that killed its predecessor: a scratch copy with the whole-file pin re-pointed. I could not. Falsity is caught where removal used to be the only trigger; the seals close the append channel at every normative position and the instrument publishes, and reproduces, the exact boundary of where they do not; the census constants genuinely derive from the artifact - I found no Python literal describing the subject anywhere in the file; and the ten escapes that rejected check-delivery-v4.py are all refused, which I confirmed both through the built-in suite and independently. Six advisories, none blocking, two of them one-line fixes (A1, A3). The verdict is ACCEPT-STANDING for the instrument, bound to c70f1533..., and nothing more: delivery.v5 stays where its own review put it, the section 7.1 disqualifier stays at full strength, the freeze row stays untouched, and the release-fixture skew stays open, now characterized in bytes at fixtureSkewMeasured for the coordinator's successor-or-disposition decision.
